purpose: Execution of chapter 6 of the UNIDROIT Principles of International Commercial Contracts (2016 edition): performance of obligations — time, performance at one time, partial and earlier performance, order of performance, place, form of payment and transfer of funds, currency, costs, imputation of payments, public permission (art. 6.1.1–6.1.17) — and hardship: the contract is to be observed, the definition of hardship and its effects up to termination or adaptation of the contract by a court (art. 6.2.1–6.2.3). The types for party, contract, term and the organ of evaluative elements come from the hub `unidroit.picc`. The list of questions and boundaries is in analysis/questions.json and QUESTIONS.md.
limitations: THIS IS NOT THE LAW OF A STATE. The Principles apply when the parties have agreed on them, or when a court or arbitral tribunal takes them as general principles of law; they do not replace the mandatory rules of the applicable law (article 1.4, hub `unidroit.picc`).

HARDSHIP IS WHAT THE CONVENTION DOES NOT HAVE AS A RULE. Article 79 of the Convention knows an exemption from liability for an impediment beyond control, but provides for neither renegotiation nor adaptation of the contract by a court. Articles 6.2.1–6.2.3 give both; on the same facts the two instruments answer differently, and this is observed by case 04.

THE EVALUATIVE ELEMENTS OF CHAPTER 6 GO THROUGH THE §47.3 JUDGMENT CHANNEL with the organ `Tribunal`: the absence of a legitimate interest of the obligee in refusing performance (6.1.3, 6.1.5), the reasonableness of upholding the remaining contract where a permission affects some terms only (6.1.16, 6.1.17), a fundamental alteration of the equilibrium of the contract and the impossibility of taking the events into account at the time of conclusion (6.2.2), the reasonableness of termination or adaptation (6.2.3(4)). The model neither decides them nor substitutes a guess.

THE RATE OF EXCHANGE AND THE CONTENT OF A PUBLIC PERMISSION ARE INPUTS OF THE CASE: articles 6.1.9 and 6.1.14–6.1.17 name the RULE OF CHOICE (which rate applies, who is to take the measures necessary to obtain the permission), while the number itself and the requirements of a particular state are brought by the case.

THE ORDER OF IMPUTATION IS WRITTEN AS §116 PRIORITIES, NOT AS READING ORDER: expenses and interest come before the obligor's indication (article 6.1.12(1)), and the four criteria of paragraph 3 displace one another in the order the source declares. Proportional imputation where no criterion applies is not in the model: that is arithmetic over an indeterminate set of debts, and no case presents it.
THE PRINCIPLES HAVE NO CALENDAR: the "reasonable time" of article 6.1.1(c) is not converted into days by the model — it remains an evaluative element or a fact of the case.
